source.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος πολὺς ὁ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ἔλαβον τὰ βαΐα τῶν φοινίκων καὶ ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐκραύγαζον· Ὡσαννά, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου, καὶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: On the next day the crowd great the [one] having come to the feast, having heard that is coming the Jesus into Jerusalem, \v 13 took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meeting him, and were crying out, "Hosanna, blessed the [one] coming in name of Lord, and the king of the Israel."

en.L: On the next day the large crowd that had come to the feast, having heard that Jesus is coming into Jerusalem, \v 13 took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed [is] the [one] coming in [the] name of [the] Lord, and the King of Israel!"
en.B: The next day the large crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way into Jerusalem. \v 13 They took branches from the palm trees and went out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, Israel's King!"
en.R: The next day the large crowd that had come for the Passover festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem. \v 13 So they took branches from the palm trees and went out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They kept shouting, "Hosanna! Praise God! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! He is the King of Israel!"

es.L: Al día siguiente, la gran multitud que había venido a la fiesta, al oír que Jesús venía a Jerusalén, \v 13 tomó ramas de las palmeras y salió a recibirlo, y gritaban: «¡Hosanna! ¡Bendito el que viene en [el] nombre del Señor, y el Rey de Israel!».
es.B: Al día siguiente, la gran multitud que había venido a la fiesta oyó que Jesús venía de camino a Jerusalén. \v 13 Tomaron ramas de palmera y salieron a recibirlo, gritando: «¡Hosanna! ¡Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor, el Rey de Israel!».
es.R: Al día siguiente, la gran multitud que había venido para la fiesta de la Pascua oyó que Jesús iba camino a Jerusalén. \v 13 Entonces tomaron ramas de palmera y salieron a recibirlo. Gritaban sin parar: «¡Hosanna! ¡Gloria a Dios! ¡Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor! ¡Él es el Rey de Israel!».

fr.L: Le lendemain, la grande foule qui était venue à la fête, ayant appris que Jésus vient à Jérusalem, \v 13 prit les rameaux des palmiers et sortit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre, et ils criaient : « Hosanna ! Béni [soit] celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur, et le roi d’Israël ! »
fr.B: Le lendemain, la grande foule venue pour la fête apprit que Jésus était en route vers Jérusalem. \v 13 Ces gens prirent des branches de palmier et sortirent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Ils criaient : « Hosanna ! Béni soit celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur, le roi d’Israël ! »
fr.R: Le lendemain, la grande foule venue pour la fête de la Pâque a appris que Jésus arrivait à Jérusalem. \v 13 Alors ces gens ont pris des branches de palmier et ils sont sortis à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Ils n’arrêtaient pas de crier : « Hosanna ! Gloire à Dieu ! Béni soit celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur ! Il est le roi d’Israël ! »

sw.L: Kesho yake umati mkubwa uliokuja kwenye sikukuu, waliposikia kwamba Yesu anakuja Yerusalemu, \v 13 walichukua matawi ya mitende, wakatoka kwenda kumlaki, wakawa wakipaza sauti, "Hosana! [Amebarikiwa] anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana, naye Mfalme wa Israeli!"
sw.B: Kesho yake umati mkubwa uliokuja kwa ajili ya sikukuu ulisikia kwamba Yesu yuko njiani kuja Yerusalemu. \v 13 Wakachukua matawi ya mitende, wakatoka kwenda kumlaki. Walikuwa wakipaza sauti, "Hosana! Amebarikiwa yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana, Mfalme wa Israeli!"
sw.R: Kesho yake umati mkubwa uliokuja kwa ajili ya sikukuu ya Pasaka ulisikia kwamba Yesu anakuja Yerusalemu. \v 13 Basi walichukua matawi ya mitende, wakatoka kwenda kumlaki. Wakaendelea kupaza sauti, "Hosana! Msifuni Mungu! Amebarikiwa yeye anayekuja kwa jina la Bwana! Yeye ndiye Mfalme wa Israeli!"

vi.L: Ngày hôm sau, đám đông lớn đã đến dự lễ, nghe rằng Đức Giê-xu đang đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, \v 13 thì lấy những tàu lá cây chà là và ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ reo hò: "Hô-sa-na! Đáng chúc tụng [thay] Đấng đến trong danh [của] Chúa, là Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.B: Hôm sau, đám đông lớn đến dự lễ nghe tin Đức Giê-xu đang trên đường vào Giê-ru-sa-lem. \v 13 Họ lấy những tàu lá chà là và ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ reo hò: "Hô-sa-na! Chúc tụng Đấng đến trong danh Chúa, là Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.R: Hôm sau, đám đông lớn đến dự Lễ Vượt Qua nghe tin Đức Giê-xu đang đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. \v 13 Vì thế họ cầm những tàu lá chà là và ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ cứ reo hò: "Hô-sa-na! Ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời! Chúc tụng Đấng đến trong danh Chúa! Đấng ấy là Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên!"

ko.L: 이튿날, 명절에 온 큰 무리가 예수께서 예루살렘으로 오신다는 것을 듣고, \v 13 종려나무 가지들을 들고 그분을 맞으러 나가서 외치고 있었다. "호산나! 주님의 이름으로 오시는 분, 곧 이스라엘의 왕께 복이 있기를!"
ko.B: 이튿날, 명절을 지키러 온 큰 무리는 예수께서 예루살렘으로 오고 계신다는 소식을 들었다. \v 13 그들은 종려나무 가지를 들고 그분을 맞으러 나가서 외쳤다. "호산나! 주님의 이름으로 오시는 분, 이스라엘의 왕께 복이 있기를!"
ko.R: 다음 날, 유월절을 지키러 온 많은 사람들이 예수께서 예루살렘으로 오신다는 소식을 들었다. \v 13 그래서 그들은 종려나무 가지를 들고 예수님을 맞으러 나갔다. 그들은 계속 외쳤다. "호산나! 하나님을 찬양하라! 주님의 이름으로 오시는 분께 복이 있기를! 그분은 이스라엘의 왕이시다!"

decisions.choice: Hosanna: a Hebrew cry, "save, please", which had become a shout of praise and welcome
alternatives: a plain plea for rescue, "save us"
decisions.reason: The word comes from Psalm 118:25, "Save us, we pray, O LORD". Psalm 118 belongs to the Hallel psalms (113-118), sung at the great festivals, Passover among them, so the cry was well known to pilgrims. By this time it was used to acclaim God and the one he sends, as here, where it stands with "Blessed is ..." rather than with a request. The old sense, a call on God to save, still lies behind it, and fits a crowd that hopes for its king.

decisions.choice: the crowd's words quote Psalm 118:25-26
decisions.reason: In the psalm the words welcome the one who comes up to the house of the LORD, and the priests answer with a blessing from the temple (Psalm 118:26). The crowd uses the festival's own psalm to welcome Jesus as he comes into the city. Matthew 21:9, Mark 11:9-10 and Luke 19:38 give the same cry.

decisions.choice: in the name of the Lord: sent by God and coming with his authority; in Psalm 118:26 "Lord" stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Psalm 118:26 the word is the divine name. To come in someone's name is to come as that person's representative. Jesus says he has come in his Father's name and does his works in it (5:43; 10:25), so the acclaim is truer than the crowd knows.

decisions.choice: "the King of Israel" is the crowd's addition to the psalm
decisions.reason: Psalm 118 does not have these words. Zephaniah 3:15 calls the LORD "the King of Israel" in the midst of Jerusalem, and the next verse tells Zion not to fear, words John's quotation echoes in verse 15. Nathanael gave Jesus the same title (1:49); after the feeding of the five thousand the crowd wanted to make him king by force (6:15), and the cross will carry the title "King of the Jews" (19:19).

decisions.choice: and: "that is", naming the one who comes
alternatives: and: a second person, besides the one who comes
decisions.reason: The one who comes and the King of Israel are the same person, Jesus. The joining word adds a title, not a second figure.

decisions.choice: palm branches: a sign of national rejoicing and victory
alternatives: ordinary green branches, with no special meaning
decisions.reason: Palms were carried in Jewish celebrations: when Simon entered the citadel of Jerusalem in triumph (1 Maccabees 13:51), and when the temple was cleansed and rededicated (2 Maccabees 10:7); palm branches were also used at the Feast of Tabernacles (Leviticus 23:40). Waving them before Jesus greets him as a victorious king. John alone says the branches were from palm trees.

decisions.choice: went out to meet him: the formal welcome given to an arriving ruler
decisions.reason: In the ancient world a city's people went out along the road to greet a king or other great visitor and escort him in. The crowd gives Jesus that kind of welcome.

decisions.choice: Hosanna (every level); Readable adds "Praise God!"
decisions.reason: "Hosanna" is the word the crowd shouted and is known from worship, so every level keeps it. Readable adds "Praise God!" to show how the shout was used (meaning decision m1). It does not translate the word's origin, "save, please", which a reader would take as a call for help.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: As at 1:23: the style guide keeps "the LORD" for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Here the Gospel quotes the psalm with the Greek word "Lord"; meaning decision m3 says whom it means. The reader's divine-name setting is not used in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (to meet him); no setting on "the one who comes" or "the King of Israel"
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Jesus and takes the setting. "The one who comes" and "the King of Israel" also mean Jesus, as the narrator shows in verses 14-16, but they are a noun phrase and a title, not pronouns, so no setting applies. In Readable "He is the King of Israel" starts a sentence and is written plain.

decisions.choice: the Passover festival
decisions.reason: The festival is the Passover named in 11:55 and 12:1; Readable names it. Balanced says "festival" for the Greek word for a feast day, which English readers might take to mean a meal.

decisions.choice: ¡Hosanna! (every level); Readable adds ¡Gloria a Dios!
decisions.reason: As in English: the cry keeps its own word, and Readable adds what it had come to mean (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el Señor
decisions.reason: In Psalm 118:26 "Lord" stands for God's own name (meaning decision m3); Spanish Bibles use "el Señor" for it.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level; Literal keeps "vient" in the report of what the crowd heard
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (12:12-19). The passé simple ("prit", "sortirent") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("ont pris"), as French is spoken and read in school. The imperfect ("criaient", "rendait témoignage") is kept at every level for what went on. In verse 12 Greek keeps the tense of the news as it was heard ("Jesus is coming"); Literal keeps that present, Balanced and Readable shift it into the past as French reported speech does.

decisions.choice: Béni [soit] celui qui vient (L); Béni soit celui qui vient (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the blessing. French says a blessing with "soit" ("Béni soit ..."), which is a wish and a praise at once, as the psalm's words are; "est béni" would turn them into a statement. Literal brackets the supplied verb.

decisions.choice: les rameaux des palmiers (L); des branches de palmier (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek article and "rameaux", the word French readers know from this scene; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "branches de palmier", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Hosana; Bwana
decisions.reason: "Hosana" is kept at every level, as the English keeps "Hosanna"; it is the word Swahili readers know from Palm Sunday. Readable adds "Msifuni Mungu" (Praise God) for its meaning as a cry of praise. "Bwana" here stands for God, as in Psalm 118.

decisions.choice: "Hô-sa-na"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew cry is kept in the familiar Vietnamese transliteration, as the English keeps "Hosanna"; Readable adds "Ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời!" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Đấng đến" for "the one coming"
decisions.reason: "Đấng" is the respectful classifier for a person honoured as sent by God; the crowd is welcoming a king in the words of the psalm.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific -si- and 께서 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "...께 복이 있기를!" for "blessed"
decisions.reason: A modern wish of blessing that a crowd could shout; the older formulas are archaic or follow the wording of familiar Korean versions.

source.text: εὑρὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὀνάριον ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτό, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον·

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu tìm được một con lừa con và ngồi lên, đúng như Kinh Thánh chép:
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu tìm được một con lừa con và cưỡi lên. Việc này xảy ra đúng như Kinh Thánh đã nói trước:

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서는 어린 나귀를 찾아서 그 위에 앉으셨다. 이것은 다음과 같이 기록된 대로였다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 어린 나귀를 찾아 그 위에 앉으셨다. 성경에 기록된 그대로였다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 어린 나귀 한 마리를 찾아 그 위에 타셨다. 이것은 성경에 미리 기록된 그대로 일어난 일이었다.

decisions.choice: young donkey
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive of the word for donkey. Diminutives of this kind often lost their force, but verse 15 calls the animal "a donkey's colt", so a young animal is meant.

decisions.choice: riding a donkey: royal, but not warlike
decisions.reason: Donkeys and mules were ridden by Israel's leaders and kings in peace: Solomon rode David's mule to be anointed king (1 Kings 1:33-38), and judges had sons riding donkeys (Judges 10:4; 12:14). A conqueror came on a war horse. By choosing a donkey, Jesus accepts the welcome as king, and shows what kind of king he is (meaning decision m3 on verse 15).

decisions.choice: Jesus found a donkey and sat on it after the crowd had come out to greet him
decisions.reason: John tells the story briefly and in a different order from the other Gospels, where the disciples fetch the animal before the crowd's acclaim (Mark 11:1-10; Matthew 21:1-9; Luke 19:29-38). Here the crowd hails him first, and then Jesus mounts the donkey. His action may be meant as an answer to their welcome: he is their king, but not a king of war. The order is clear; how much John means by it is less certain.

decisions.choice: just as Scripture says (B); This was just what the Scriptures had said would happen (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a quotation from Scripture, and the tense means that the words stand written and still hold. Balanced and Readable name Scripture, since "it is written" alone may not tell a modern reader that a Bible quotation follows. Literal keeps the Greek form.

decisions.choice: asnillo (L); burrito (B, R)
decisions.reason: A young donkey. "Burrito" is the everyday word and carries no comic note in this sense.

source.text: Μὴ φοβοῦ, θυγάτηρ Σιών· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται, καθήμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου.

records.literal_gloss: Not be afraid, daughter of Zion; behold, the king of you is coming, sitting on a colt of a donkey.

en.L: "Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion; look, your king is coming, sitting on a colt of a donkey."
en.B: "Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion! Look, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey's colt."
en.R: "People of Jerusalem, do not be afraid! Look! Your king is coming, riding on a young donkey!"

es.L: «No temas, hija de Sion; mira, tu rey viene, sentado sobre un pollino de asna».
es.B: «¡No temas, hija de Sion! Mira, tu rey viene, montado en la cría de un asna».
es.R: «¡Habitantes de Jerusalén, no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo! ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}! ¡{{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} rey viene montado en un burrito!».

fr.L: « N’aie pas peur, fille de Sion ; regarde, ton roi vient, assis sur le petit d’un âne. »
fr.B: « N’aie pas peur, fille de Sion ! Regarde : ton roi vient, monté sur un ânon. »
fr.R: « Habitants de Jérusalem, n’ayez pas peur ! Regardez ! Votre roi arrive, monté sur un jeune âne ! »

sw.L: "Usiogope, binti Sayuni; tazama, mfalme wako anakuja, ameketi juu ya mwana-punda."
sw.B: "Usiogope, binti Sayuni! Tazama, mfalme wako anakuja, ameketi juu ya mwana-punda."
sw.R: "Watu wa Yerusalemu, msiogope! Tazameni! Mfalme wenu anakuja, amepanda mwana-punda!"

vi.L: "Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, đừng sợ; kìa, vua của ngươi đang đến, ngồi trên lừa con."
vi.B: "Hỡi con gái Si-ôn, đừng sợ! Kìa, vua của ngươi đang đến, ngồi trên lưng lừa con."
vi.R: "Hỡi người dân Giê-ru-sa-lem, đừng sợ! Hãy xem kìa! Vua của các ngươi đang đến, cưỡi trên một con lừa con!"

ko.L: "두려워하지 마라, 시온의 딸아. 보아라, 네 왕이 오신다, 나귀의 새끼 위에 앉으셔서."
ko.B: "시온의 딸아, 겁내지 마라! 보아라, 네 왕이 어린 나귀 위에 앉아서 오신다."
ko.R: "예루살렘 사람들아, 두려워하지 마라! 보아라! 너희 왕이 어린 나귀를 타고 오신다!"

decisions.choice: the quotation is from Zechariah 9:9, shortened
decisions.reason: Zechariah 9:9 reads, "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you, righteous and bringing salvation, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey." John keeps the king and the donkey and leaves out the rest. Matthew 21:5 quotes the same verse.

decisions.choice: "Do not be afraid" in place of Zechariah's "Rejoice greatly": most likely from Zephaniah 3:16
alternatives: Isaiah 40:9 ("do not fear ... Here is your God")
John's own wording, with no second passage in mind
decisions.reason: Zephaniah 3:14-16 tells the daughter of Zion to rejoice because "the King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst", and says to Jerusalem, "Do not fear, Zion." The crowd has just used the title King of Israel (verse 13), which makes Zephaniah a likely source. Isaiah 40:9 also tells Zion not to fear and announces God's coming. John does not say which passage he has in mind.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people
alternatives: a young woman of the city
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of Jerusalem as a woman, "daughter Zion" (Isaiah 1:8; Zechariah 9:9). Zion is the hill of the city and the temple, and the phrase stands for the whole city and the people who live there.

decisions.choice: a king who comes in peace, not on a war horse
decisions.reason: The next verse of Zechariah says that God will cut off the chariot and the war horse from Jerusalem, and that the king will speak peace to the nations (Zechariah 9:10). The donkey is part of that picture. The king John's readers see is the one who will be lifted up on the cross (12:32-33) and whose kingdom is not from this world (18:36).

decisions.choice: a donkey's colt: one young donkey
alternatives: two animals, a donkey and its colt
decisions.reason: Zechariah's Hebrew names the animal twice in parallel lines, "on a donkey, on a colt". Matthew 21:2-7 tells of two animals; John speaks of one, the young donkey of verse 14.

decisions.choice: People of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m3), since a young reader would take "daughter" as one girl. Literal and Balanced keep the prophet's phrase.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: The word calls for attention. The style guide does not use "behold". There is no setting on "your" or "your king": "your" refers to the city, and "king" is a noun, not a pronoun for Jesus.

decisions.choice: Habitantes de Jerusalén
decisions.reason: As in English: says who "the daughter of Zion" is (meaning decision m3). Addressed to many, so Readable's "you" takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: tu to "fille de Sion" (L, B); vous to "Habitants de Jérusalem" (R)
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to the city as one woman, "daughter of Zion", in the singular, so Literal and Balanced say "tu". Readable names the people of the city instead (meaning decision m3, as the English Readable does), and a group takes "vous".

decisions.choice: regarde (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Voici" is a possible rendering of the Greek word, but "regarde" keeps the call for attention addressed to the city, as "look" does in the English, and it does not echo older French versions.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" / "các ngươi" for Zion addressed in the prophecy
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks for God to the city; "ngươi" is the usual form for that solemn address in Vietnamese Bibles and is not rude in this register.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the Greek order: the command before the address, and "sitting on a donkey's colt" after the verb
alternatives: 시온의 딸아, 두려워하지 마라. 보아라, 네 왕이 나귀 새끼를 타고 오신다.
decisions.reason: Following the Greek's order keeps Literal close to the source and away from the familiar wording of the standard Korean versions.

source.text: ταῦτα οὐκ ἔγνωσαν αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ τὸ πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ ὅτε ἐδοξάσθη Ἰησοῦς τότε ἐμνήσθησαν ὅτι ταῦτα ἦν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα καὶ ταῦτα ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: These things not understood of him the disciples at the first, but when was glorified Jesus, then they remembered that these things were about him having been written and these things they did to him.

en.L: These things {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples did not understand at the first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and [that] they had done these things to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: At first {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples did not understand what these things meant. But when Jesus had been glorified, they remembered that these things had been written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that they had done these very things for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: At first {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples did not understand what all this meant. But later Jesus was glorified through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death and resurrection. Then they remembered that Scripture had said these things about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that they had done these very things for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Estas cosas no las entendieron sus discípulos al principio; pero cuando Jesús fue glorificado, entonces se acordaron de que estas cosas estaban escritas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y [de que] se las habían hecho a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Al principio sus discípulos no entendieron lo que significaban estas cosas. Pero cuando Jesús fue glorificado, se acordaron de que estas cosas se habían escrito acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y de que eso era precisamente lo que habían hecho por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Al principio sus discípulos no entendieron lo que significaba todo esto. Pero más tarde Jesús fue glorificado por medio de su muerte y su resurrección. Entonces se acordaron de que las Escrituras decían estas cosas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y de que eso era precisamente lo que habían hecho por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Ces choses, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ne [les] comprirent pas d’abord, mais quand Jésus fut glorifié, alors ils se souvinrent que ces choses étaient écrites à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet et [qu’]ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avaient fait ces choses.
fr.B: Au début, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ne comprirent pas le sens de ces événements. Mais quand Jésus eut été glorifié, ils se souvinrent que cela avait été écrit à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet, et que c’était justement ce qu’on avait fait pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Au début, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples n’ont pas compris ce que tout cela voulait dire. Mais plus tard, Jésus a été glorifié par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} résurrection. Alors ils se sont souvenus que les Écritures avaient dit cela à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet, et que c’était justement ce qu’on avait fait pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Mambo haya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hawakuyaelewa hapo kwanza, lakini Yesu alipotukuzwa, ndipo walipokumbuka kwamba mambo haya yalikuwa yameandikwa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na [kwamba] walimtendea mambo haya.
sw.B: Mwanzoni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hawakuelewa maana ya mambo haya. Lakini Yesu alipokwisha kutukuzwa, walikumbuka kwamba mambo haya yalikuwa yameandikwa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na kwamba walikuwa wamemtendea mambo hayo hayo.
sw.R: Mwanzoni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hawakuelewa maana ya mambo hayo yote. Lakini baadaye Yesu alitukuzwa kupitia kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} na ufufuo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Ndipo walipokumbuka kwamba Maandiko yalikuwa yamesema mambo haya juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na kwamba walikuwa wamemtendea mambo hayo hayo.

vi.L: Lúc đầu, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không hiểu những điều này, nhưng khi Đức Giê-xu đã được tôn vinh, bấy giờ họ mới nhớ lại rằng những điều này đã được chép về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và [rằng] người ta đã làm những điều này cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lúc đầu, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không hiểu ý nghĩa những việc này. Nhưng khi Đức Giê-xu đã được tôn vinh, họ mới nhớ lại rằng những điều này đã được chép về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và người ta đã làm đúng những việc ấy cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Lúc đầu, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không hiểu ý nghĩa của mọi việc này. Nhưng về sau, Đức Giê-xu được tôn vinh qua sự chết và sự sống lại của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bấy giờ họ mới nhớ lại rằng Kinh Thánh đã nói những điều này về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và người ta đã làm đúng những việc ấy cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 이 일들을 그분의 제자들은 처음에는 깨닫지 못했으나, 예수께서 영광스럽게 되셨을 때에, 그때에 이 일들이 그분에 관하여 기록된 것이었고 그들이 이 일들을 그분께 해 드렸다는 것을 기억했다.
ko.B: 제자들은 처음에는 이 일들이 무슨 뜻인지 깨닫지 못했다. 그러나 예수께서 영광스럽게 되신 뒤에, 이것이 그분에 대해 기록된 말씀이었고 그들이 바로 그대로 그분께 해 드렸다는 것을 기억했다.
ko.R: 처음에 예수님의 제자들은 이 모든 일이 무슨 뜻인지 몰랐다. 그러나 나중에 예수께서 죽으시고 다시 살아나셔서 영광스럽게 되셨다. 그제야 제자들은 성경이 예수님에 대해 바로 이 일들을 말했다는 것과, 그들이 바로 그대로 예수님께 해 드렸다는 것을 기억했다.

decisions.choice: did not understand: did not grasp what the events meant
alternatives: did not know: were unaware of what happened
decisions.reason: The disciples saw all of it. What they did not see at the time was that the welcome and the donkey fulfilled Scripture and showed who Jesus was.

decisions.choice: was glorified: Jesus's death, resurrection and return to the Father, seen as one event
decisions.reason: In John, Jesus is glorified in his "hour": the Son of Man is glorified when, like a grain of wheat, he dies and bears fruit (12:23-24; 13:31-32), and he returns to the glory he had with the Father (17:1, 5). The Spirit was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified (7:39). The passive points to God as the one who glorifies him (17:1).

decisions.choice: the disciples understood only after Jesus was glorified
decisions.reason: John says the same in 2:22, after the resurrection, and Jesus promises that the Spirit will remind the disciples of all he said (14:26). The light of Easter showed them that Scripture had spoken of these things.

decisions.choice: they had done these things to him: "they" left general, the people who welcomed him, the disciples perhaps among them
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is the disciples, who remembered. But in John it is the crowd that went out with palm branches and shouted, and Jesus himself found the donkey. John may use "they" loosely for those who took part, as the other Gospels have the disciples fetching the animal and joining the shout (Luke 19:35-37). Every level keeps "they".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Each pronoun refers to Jesus and takes the setting.

decisions.choice: for him
decisions.reason: What was done was an honor: the welcome, the branches and the acclaim. In English "done to him" can sound like harm, so Balanced and Readable say "for him". Literal keeps "to him".

decisions.choice: glorified through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death and resurrection
decisions.reason: Readable says what "glorified" refers to here (meaning decision m2), since a young reader would not know. The return to the Father belongs to the same glory (17:5); the death and resurrection are named because they are what made the disciples remember (2:22).

decisions.choice: por él
decisions.reason: As in English: what was done was done for him, in welcome.

decisions.choice: ce qu’on avait fait pour lui (B, R); ils lui avaient fait (L)
alternatives: ce qu’ils avaient fait pour lui (B, R)
decisions.reason: John leaves "they" general: the people who welcomed Jesus, the disciples perhaps among them (meaning decision m4). After "ils se souvinrent", a second "ils" would point at the disciples alone; French "on" keeps the subject open. Literal keeps the Greek plural.

decisions.choice: "người ta" for "they had done"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves "they" general; Vietnamese "họ" would point back to the disciples, so the impersonal "người ta" keeps it open.

decisions.choice: 영광스럽게 되셨다 for the passive "was glorified"
decisions.reason: The guide's key term is 영광스럽게 하다; its passive keeps the same word so the thread of "glorify" stays visible through John.

decisions.choice: 그들이 ("they") left general
decisions.reason: 사람들이 would exclude the disciples and 자기들이 would point only to them; 그들이 leaves "they" as open as the Greek, as the meaning decision asks.

source.text: ἐμαρτύρει οὖν ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ὢν μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὅτε τὸν Λάζαρον ἐφώνησεν ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου καὶ ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Was testifying therefore the crowd the [one] being with him when the Lazarus he called out of the tomb and raised him out of dead [ones].

en.L: So the crowd that was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him out of [the] dead was testifying.
en.B: Meanwhile the crowd that had been with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Lazarus out of his tomb and raised him from the dead kept on testifying to what they had seen.
en.R: The people who had been with Jesus when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Lazarus out of the tomb and brought him back to life kept telling others what they had seen.

es.L: Daba testimonio, pues, la multitud que estaba con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} cuando llamó a Lázaro del sepulcro y lo resucitó de [los] muertos.
es.B: Mientras tanto, la multitud que había estado con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} cuando llamó a Lázaro del sepulcro y lo resucitó de entre los muertos seguía dando testimonio de lo que había visto.
es.R: La gente que había estado con Jesús cuando llamó a Lázaro de la tumba y lo hizo volver a la vida seguía contándoles a otros lo que había visto.

fr.L: La foule qui était avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appela Lazare hors du tombeau et le ressuscita des morts rendait donc témoignage.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, la foule qui avait été avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait appelé Lazare hors de son tombeau et l’avait ressuscité des morts continuait à rendre témoignage de ce qu’elle avait vu.
fr.R: Les gens qui étaient avec Jésus quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait appelé Lazare à sortir du tombeau et l’avait ramené à la vie racontaient à tout le monde ce qu’ils avaient vu.

sw.L: Basi umati uliokuwa pamoja naye alipomwita Lazaro kutoka kaburini na kumfufua kutoka kwa wafu ulikuwa ukishuhudia.
sw.B: Wakati huo umati uliokuwa pamoja naye alipomwita Lazaro kutoka kaburini na kumfufua kutoka kwa wafu uliendelea kushuhudia yale waliyoyaona.
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa pamoja na Yesu alipomwita Lazaro kutoka kaburini na kumrudisha uhai waliendelea kuwaeleza wengine yale waliyoyaona.

vi.L: Vậy đám đông đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi La-xa-rơ ra khỏi mộ và khiến ông sống lại từ [cõi] chết, cứ làm chứng.
vi.B: Trong khi đó, đám đông đã ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi La-xa-rơ ra khỏi mộ và khiến ông sống lại từ cõi chết, cứ làm chứng về những gì họ đã thấy.
vi.R: Những người đã ở với Đức Giê-xu lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi La-xa-rơ ra khỏi mộ và cho ông sống lại, cứ kể cho người khác nghe những gì họ đã thấy.

ko.L: 그러므로 그분이 나사로를 무덤에서 불러내어 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살리실 때에 그분과 함께 있던 무리가 증언하고 있었다.
ko.B: 한편, 예수께서 나사로를 무덤에서 불러내어 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살리실 때 함께 있었던 무리는, 자기들이 본 것을 계속 증언했다.
ko.R: 예수께서 나사로를 무덤에서 불러내어 다시 살리실 때 그 자리에 있었던 사람들은, 자기들이 본 것을 다른 사람들에게 계속 이야기했다.

decisions.choice: when (hote; SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, read "when": the crowd who were with him when he called Lazarus kept testifying. Some, including an early papyrus and Codex Bezae, read "that": the crowd who were with him kept testifying that he had called Lazarus from the tomb. The two words differ by one letter, and the sense is close. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: kept testifying: the imperfect tense, an ongoing witness
decisions.reason: The tense shows continuing action: they went on telling what they had seen. Testifying is a key theme in John: John the Baptist, the works of Jesus, the Scriptures and the Father all testify to him (1:7; 5:31-39). These eyewitnesses are added to them.

decisions.choice: this crowd: the people who had been at Bethany, not the festival crowd of verse 12
alternatives: the same crowd as in verses 12 and 18
decisions.reason: John describes this crowd as the people who were with Jesus at the tomb (11:42, 45). The crowd in verse 18 is the one that "had heard" of the sign, the pilgrims of verse 12. The first group's testimony is why the second went out to meet him.

decisions.choice: raised: Jesus raised Lazarus (active)
decisions.reason: The verb is active, with Jesus as subject, as in 12:1, 9: he is the resurrection and the life (11:25). Contrast 2:22, where Jesus himself "was raised".

decisions.choice: testifying to what they had seen (B); kept telling others what they had seen (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object; Balanced and Readable say what the crowd testified to, the raising of Lazarus they had seen. Readable uses plain words for "testify". Literal keeps the verb alone.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The pronouns that refer to Jesus take the setting; "him" for Lazarus does not. Readable writes "with Jesus" so that the two men are not confused, and "brought him back to life" for "raised him from the dead".

decisions.choice: seguía dando testimonio de lo que había visto (B); seguía contándoles a otros (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows that the witness went on (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: racontaient à tout le monde ce qu’ils avaient vu (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, which says "kept telling others": "rendre témoignage" is church language for a young reader, and the sense here is that they kept telling what they had seen (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep "rendre témoignage", the key word of John.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι ἤκουσαν τοῦτο αὐτὸν πεποιηκέναι τὸ σημεῖον.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this also met him the crowd, because they heard this him to have done the sign.

en.L: Because of this also the crowd met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because they heard [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done this sign.
en.B: That was also why the crowd went out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: they had heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done this sign.
en.R: This is also why the crowd came out to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They had heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done this sign, raising Lazarus from death.

es.L: Por esto también la multitud le salió al encuentro, porque oyeron que había hecho esta señal.
es.B: Por eso también la multitud salió a recibirlo: habían oído que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho esta señal.
es.R: Por eso también la multitud salió a recibirlo. Habían oído que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho esta señal: resucitar a Lázaro.

fr.L: C’est pour cela aussi que la foule vint à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre, parce qu’ils avaient appris [qu’]{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait ce signe.
fr.B: C’est aussi pour cela que la foule sortit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre : ces gens avaient appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait ce signe.
fr.R: C’est aussi pour cela que la foule est sortie à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Les gens avaient appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait ce signe en ramenant Lazare de la mort à la vie.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii pia umati ulikwenda kumlaki, kwa kuwa walisikia kwamba alikuwa ameifanya ishara hii.
sw.B: Hiyo pia ndiyo sababu umati ulitoka kwenda kumlaki: walikuwa wamesikia kwamba alikuwa ameifanya ishara hii.
sw.R: Hii pia ndiyo sababu umati ulitoka kwenda kumlaki. Walikuwa wamesikia kwamba alikuwa ameifanya ishara hii, ya kumfufua Lazaro kutoka kwa wafu.

vi.L: Cũng vì điều này mà đám đông ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì họ nghe [rằng] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm dấu lạ này.
vi.B: Đó cũng là lý do đám đông ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: họ đã nghe rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm dấu lạ này.
vi.R: Đây cũng là lý do đám đông ra đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ đã nghe rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm dấu lạ này, là cho La-xa-rơ sống lại từ cõi chết.

ko.L: 이 때문에 또한 무리가 그분을 맞으러 나왔는데, 그분이 이 표적을 행하셨다는 것을 들었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 무리가 예수를 맞으러 나온 것도 이 때문이었다. 그분이 이 표적을 행하셨다는 소식을 들었던 것이다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 예수님을 맞으러 나온 것도 이 때문이었다. 예수께서 나사로를 죽음에서 살리신 이 표적을 행하셨다는 이야기를 들었던 것이다.

decisions.choice: because of this ... because: the reason is given by the clause that follows
alternatives: "this" pointing back to the testimony of verse 17
decisions.reason: "This" points forward to "because they heard": hearing of the sign is why they came. "Also" adds this reason to what verse 17 has said, and the two verses together show the testimony spreading from one crowd to the other.

decisions.choice: the crowd: the festival crowd of verse 12; "they" heard
decisions.reason: The crowd is singular but "they heard" is plural: John thinks of the many people in it. These are the pilgrims who went out with palm branches (verses 12-13), and their reason is now given.

decisions.choice: this sign: the raising of Lazarus
decisions.reason: The raising of Lazarus is the last and greatest sign in John before Jesus's hour. It shows him as the resurrection and the life (11:25-26). It also led the council to plan his death (11:47-53), so the sign that brings the crowd out to meet him is the sign that leads to the cross.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Each pronoun refers to Jesus and takes the setting. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain.

decisions.choice: raising Lazarus from death
decisions.reason: Readable names the sign (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: resucitar a Lázaro
decisions.reason: As in English: names the sign (meaning decision m3).

source.text: οἱ οὖν Φαρισαῖοι εἶπαν πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Θεωρεῖτε ὅτι οὐκ ὠφελεῖτε οὐδέν· ἴδε ὁ κόσμος ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Pharisees said to themselves, "You see that not you are gaining nothing; look, the world after him went away."

en.L: So the Pharisees said to one another, "You see that you are gaining nothing at all; look, the world has gone off after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: So the Pharisees said to one another, "You can see for yourselves that you are getting nowhere. Look, the whole world has gone off after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: So the Pharisees said to each other, "You can see that nothing you do is working. Look, the whole world is following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

es.L: Los fariseos, pues, dijeron entre sí: «{{plural_you:Ya ven|Ya veis}} que no {{plural_you:ganan|ganáis}} nada; {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, el mundo se ha ido tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.B: Entonces los fariseos se dijeron unos a otros: «{{plural_you:Ya ven|Ya veis}} que no {{plural_you:están consiguiendo|estáis consiguiendo}} nada. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, todo el mundo se ha ido tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!».
es.R: Por eso los fariseos se decían unos a otros: «{{plural_you:Ya ven|Ya veis}} que nada de lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} funciona. ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, todo el mundo se va tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!».

fr.L: Les Pharisiens dirent donc entre eux : « Vous voyez que vous n’y gagnez rien du tout ; regardez, le monde est parti derrière {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens se dirent alors les uns aux autres : « Vous le voyez bien, vous n’arrivez à rien. Regardez : le monde entier s’est mis à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} suite ! »
fr.R: Alors les Pharisiens se sont dit entre eux : « Vous voyez bien que tout ce que vous faites ne sert à rien. Regardez, le monde entier {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suit ! »

sw.L: Basi Mafarisayo wakaambiana, "Mnaona kwamba hamfaidi kitu chochote; tazama, ulimwengu umekwenda nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.B: Basi Mafarisayo wakaambiana, "Mnaona wenyewe kwamba hamfiki popote. Tazama, ulimwengu wote umekwenda kumfuata!"
sw.R: Basi Mafarisayo wakaambiana, "Mnaona kwamba hakuna mnachofanya kinachofaulu. Tazama, ulimwengu wote unamfuata!"

vi.L: Vậy người Pha-ri-si nói với nhau: "Các ông thấy đó, các ông chẳng được ích gì cả; kìa, thế gian đã đi theo ông ta rồi."
vi.B: Vậy người Pha-ri-si nói với nhau: "Các ông tự thấy đó, các ông chẳng làm được gì cả. Kìa, cả thế gian đã chạy theo ông ta rồi!"
vi.R: Vậy người Pha-ri-si nói với nhau: "Các ông thấy đó, chúng ta làm gì cũng vô ích. Kìa, cả thiên hạ đều đi theo ông ta!"

ko.L: 그러므로 바리새파 사람들이 서로 말했다. "너희가 보다시피, 너희는 아무것도 이루지 못하고 있다. 보아라, 세상이 그를 따라가 버렸다."
ko.B: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 서로 말했다. "너희도 보다시피, 아무리 해도 소용이 없다. 보아라, 온 세상이 그를 따라가 버렸다!"
ko.R: 그래서 바리새파 사람들은 서로 말했다. "봐라, 너희가 무엇을 해도 소용이 없다. 온 세상이 그 사람을 따라가고 있다!"

decisions.choice: the world: everyone, a complaint that exaggerates
decisions.reason: The Pharisees mean that the crowds have gone over to Jesus. John lets the words say more than they intend: the world is what God loves and what Jesus came to save (3:16-17; 4:42), and in the next verse some Greeks come asking to see him (12:20-21). The council had feared the same thing, that "everyone will believe in him" (11:48), and Caiaphas, too, said more than he knew (11:49-52).

decisions.choice: you are gaining nothing: your efforts are getting you nowhere
alternatives: you are no help at all
decisions.reason: The verb means to help, benefit or gain, and the Greek doubles the negative for emphasis. The council had decided to kill Jesus and had ordered that anyone who knew where he was should report it (11:53, 57), and still the crowds went out to welcome him.

decisions.choice: You see: a statement
decisions.reason: The Greek form can be read either way, and the sense is much the same: they point to what is plain before them. The statement fits a complaint to one another.

decisions.choice: gone after him: become his followers
decisions.reason: To go after someone is to follow him as a disciple or supporter (compare 1:37; Mark 1:20). The past tense speaks as though it had already happened, which adds to the alarm of the words.

decisions.choice: the whole world
decisions.reason: "The world" is kept (key term), with "whole" added so that the line reads in English as the exaggerated complaint it is (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "the world" alone.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Jesus and takes the setting, as elsewhere in the narrative, though the speakers are his opponents.

decisions.choice: todo el mundo
decisions.reason: Spanish "todo el mundo" means everyone, which is the sense here (meaning decision m1), and still echoes "the world".

decisions.choice: le monde entier (B, R)
decisions.reason: The complaint exaggerates (meaning decision m1). French "tout le monde" would say it most naturally, but it means "everybody" and hides the key word "le monde", which John lets say more than the Pharisees intend; "le monde entier" keeps the word and the exaggeration.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" for Jesus in the Pharisees' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: His opponents would not call him "ngài"; the English span becomes a plain pronoun, as in 11:48.

decisions.choice: "cả thiên hạ" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "the world" as "everyone", an angry exaggeration; "cả thiên hạ" is the everyday Vietnamese way to say it. Literal and Balanced keep "thế gian".

decisions.choice: The Pharisees call Jesus 그 / 그 사람, without honorifics
decisions.reason: They speak of him with hostility among themselves; the narrator keeps the honorific for Jesus.
